title: Zen and Creativity Class 2 Part 1
speaker: Shuko Edie Norton
summary: Shuko Edie Norton leads a writing session in which the class composes short descriptive poems in the manner of haiku, loosening the five-seven-five form and the rhyme. Shuko describes the qualities of haiku, such as image words over abstract ones and a quick turn after the first two lines, and reads the poem The Laws of Japanese Painting. Shuko recalls listening to Japanese literature on the radio in Japan without understanding the words, then reads poems by Basho and Issa, including the old pond and the frog. Shuko plays shakuhachi music and sets out photographs, paintings, and objects in the room to prompt the writing.
